newsitem.title: INDIA: India truckers say expect to call off strike.
newsitem.headline: India truckers say expect to call off strike.

text.p: Indian truck owners said on Wednesday they expected to call off a 10-day-old strike that has crippled trade and pushed up prices because the government had met their demands.

"Our people have gone to sign the agreement with the government and if there are no last minute hitches, the strike will be called off," S.P. Singh, spokesman of the All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC), told Reuters.

"Our demand for shedding the responsibility of collecting the service tax has been met," Singh added. "The hike in insurance premium has also been kept in abeyance. It will be re-examined by the government."
At least 2.2 million vehicles stayed off the road for ten days to protest a planned five percent service tax on road transport and a sharp rise in insurance premiums.
The tax was proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his federal budget for financial year 1997/98 (April-March).
There was no immediate response from the government though government officials had said earlier on Wednesday that they expected to narrow the areas of disagreement soon.
